newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chernogorneft mulling U.S. share issue.
newsitem.headline: Chernogorneft mulling U.S. share issue.

text.p: Russian oil company AOOT Chernogorneft is planning to list its shares on the New York Stock Exchange, the company said on Thursday.
Chairman and President Boris Volkov met officials of the NYSE and U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission to discuss the listing, it said in a report on its first three quarters.
Chernogorneft is one of several Russian companies to have issued American Depositary Receipts (ADRs). Its level-one ADRs are already quoted on the NASDAQ bulletin board.
Chernogorneft has published financial figures audited to U.S. GAAP by Ernst & Young for 1994 and 1995, and the company said it would also prepare 1996 statements in this way.

Chernogorneft said its pre-tax profit in the first three quarter of this year was $53.7 million on net sales of $362.4 million, according to Russian accruals-based accounting standards, for which comparisons are not available.
As of October 1, 1996, NK Sidanko owned 37.7 percent and Uneximbank (Oneksimbank in Russian) and affiliates Bank MFK (IFCI) and Moscow Partners 14.7 percent.

Another 17.1 percent was held in American Depositary Receipts through Bank of New York, and 6.3 percent in Russian Depositary Receipts through ING Barings. Other foreign entities owned 13.0 percent, individual shareholders 7.5 percent, other Russian entities 2.0 percent, Treasury stock 1.7 percent.

The Uneximbank group has control over Chernogorneft, as Bank MFK backed by Uneximbank won control of 51 percent of Sidanko under the government's shares-for-loans programme. In September InterRos Oil acquired 34 percent of Sidanko and must transfer 13 percent of Chernogorneft to Sidanko. The Interros group includes Uneximbank and MFK.
At 1145 GMT Chernogorneft was $11.30 on the Russian Trading System, up from $11.25 at Wednesday's close.
